questions.title: Power-tuned logistic inference with independently sampled machine predictions
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted study of prediction-powered logistic-risk minimization. Labeled observations (X_i,F_i,Y_i) are iid, Y is binary, X is a fixed-dimensional bounded design vector, and F in [0,1] is the output of an external predictor fixed independently of these evaluation samples. F may use auxiliary features not in the regression vector X. Independent unlabeled pairs (X_tilde_j,F_tilde_j) have exactly the same (X,F) law; their sample size N may differ from labeled size n. The estimand beta_star minimizes expected logistic loss ell_beta(X,Y)=log(1+exp(X^T beta))-Y X^T beta. The conditional logistic model need not be correct. Study the rectified empirical objective R_lambda=mean_labeled ell(X,Y)+lambda*(mean_unlabeled ell(X,F)-mean_labeled ell(X,F)) for lambda in [0,1], including one data-estimated power-tuning step. Derive consistency, the correctly centered independent two-sample score limit, sandwich variance, marginal asymptotic 95% intervals, and the trace-minimizing population lambda in [0,1]. Establish why a consistent same-sample plug-in lambda has the same first-order limit as its population target. State identification, Hessian, moment, nondegeneracy, predictor-independence and optimizer-error conditions, and finite-sample existence/separation limitations. Distinguish minimizing total asymptotic variance from improving every coordinate or every realized interval. For the new estimator use a label-only unpenalized logistic pilot (lambda=0), one trace-based tuning step, and then a final fit at that weight; do not retune repeatedly. At the pilot use the pooled labeled/unlabeled average logistic Hessian, labeled centered cross-covariance normalized by n, and the centered covariance of all concatenated prediction scores normalized by n+N-1. Clip the scalar trace optimizer to [0,1]. At the final estimate use the pooled average Hessian and separately centered labeled residual-score and unlabeled prediction-score covariances with their respective m-1 denominators and actual sample sizes. Implement est_ppi_logistic from numerical primitives, not ppi_py or a prebuilt prediction-powered estimator. NumPy/SciPy optimizers are permitted. Useful diagnostic calculations and revisions are model choices. After independent acceptance of current theory and source, freeze at least two bounded, full-rank designs with unequal n/N, one informative and one deliberately poor external predictor, at least 1000 independent labeled/unlabeled sample pairs per design, nominal 95% marginal coverage, a coverage MCSE target <=0.01, and pre-result seeds, sample sizes, numerical tolerances and acceptance criteria. Use a justified population logistic-risk target, including under misspecification; compare coverage, bias, empirical versus estimated variance, and paired classical/tuned precision with uncertainty. Report unresolved criteria honestly without outcome-driven extension. Separately execute the pinned original ppi_py logistic CI helper through the supplied source launcher, inspect both streams and ppi_logistic_result.json, and describe numeric coverage and the exact source/environment. That launcher seeds 1000 calls to the unchanged upstream helper with original defaults n=1000,N=10000,d=1 and three alpha values. It is not the original ten-trial parallel test, a historical hardware reproduction or all paper figures. Upstream default power tuning uses a lambda=1 pilot; do not call it identical to the new label-only-pilot procedure. Source execution does not replace new implementation or fresh confirmation. Attribute source assistance rather than claiming blind rediscovery. Complete Markdown/LaTeX theory, new code, frozen confirmation, source reproduction and a final evidence report are all required. Lean and novelty are not required; no fixed research order or derivation length is imposed.

source.primary_authority: Angelopoulos, Duchi and Zrnic, PPI++: Efficient Prediction-Powered Inference, arXiv:2311.01453v2, Sections 3, 4 and 6, and the pinned MIT ppi_py implementation.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.shape: Finite n-by-d matrix with full column rank and n>d+2.
request_fields.indexing: Rows align with y and predictions; any intercept is an explicit input column.
request_fields.edge_cases: No implicit intercept or feature normalization. Tests use nonseparated regular data; report optimization failure honestly.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.edge_cases: Both classes occur in the qualification data.
request_fields.meaning: Observed labels, never replaced by predictions.

request_fields.name: predictions
request_fields.edge_cases: They need not equal the regression mean or be well calibrated.
request_fields.meaning: External predictor outputs for the labeled observations.

request_fields.name: x_unlabeled
request_fields.shape: Finite N-by-d full-rank matrix with N>d+2.
request_fields.indexing: Independent rows, not paired to the labeled sample.
request_fields.edge_cases: N need not equal n; do not concatenate samples as observed outcomes.

request_fields.name: predictions_unlabeled
request_fields.edge_cases: Same predictor and joint feature law as the labeled sample.
request_fields.meaning: External outputs on independent unlabeled observations.

request_fields.name: lambda
request_fields.indexing: One scalar for the entire vector parameter.
request_fields.edge_cases: Null requests exactly one label-only-pilot tuning step; a numeric value is used unchanged without tuning.
request_fields.meaning: Fixed objective weight or the adaptive procedure selector, not a penalty.

response_fields.name: beta
response_fields.edge_cases: No clipping, regularization or silent substitution of a population target.
response_fields.meaning: Final minimizer of the requested rectified objective.
response_fields.normalization: Use each sample's own empirical average.

response_fields.name: lambda
response_fields.edge_cases: An unidentifiable zero tuning denominator must be reported rather than disguised as estimated optimality; test designs have positive population denominator.
response_fields.meaning: Requested fixed weight or one pilot-estimated clipped trace optimizer.
response_fields.normalization: The labeled/unlabeled sample-size ratio enters the variance objective.

response_fields.name: covariance
response_fields.indexing: Input column order on both axes.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not equate a zero diagonal with a nondegenerate normal limit.
response_fields.meaning: Derived sandwich estimate of the covariance of beta, using the final fit and the declared sample-covariance conventions.
response_fields.normalization: Unscaled estimator covariance, not the covariance of sqrt(n)*(beta-beta_star). Both n and N enter.

response_fields.name: standard_errors
response_fields.edge_cases: Use the diagonal of the same returned covariance.

response_fields.name: ci_lower
response_fields.meaning: Asymptotic two-sided 95% marginal Wald lower endpoints.
response_fields.normalization: Same beta and standard errors as returned.

response_fields.name: ci_upper
response_fields.meaning: Asymptotic two-sided 95% marginal Wald upper endpoints.
response_fields.normalization: Same beta and standard errors as returned.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate inputs or access hidden data, filesystem, network, ppi_py, a prebuilt logistic-regression estimator, or a prebuilt prediction-powered estimator. General numerical optimization and matrix primitives are allowed.

All returned quantities describe the same current data, final estimate and single lambda. Numerical lambda=0 recovers the labeled logistic point estimate; input-column permutations permute beta and covariance consistently.

Use a bounded numerical solver with honest convergence diagnostics. Numerical optimization accuracy and asymptotically negligible error are separate obligations; do not claim a fixed nonzero solver error proves a CLT.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze at least two bounded full-rank designs with informative and poor predictors, unequal sample sizes, at least 1000 independent two-sample repetitions per design, seeds, tolerances, coverage precision target <=0.01 and acceptance criteria.

Assess marginal coverage, bias and covariance calibration around the justified population logistic-risk minimizer; account for both sampling sources and compare classical/tuned precision on paired datasets.

Report numerical and statistical failures, Monte Carlo uncertainty and non-novel source-assisted scope. Neither source reproduction nor simulation proves a theorem, universal finite-sample improvement or simultaneous coverage.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Finite numerical iteration limits and honest nonconvergence; no mandatory number of research revisions or scratch calls.
